origins.section: The Compiler Rejects a Case That an Earlier Case Always Wins, but It Does Not Read Guards
Over a Sealed Type, Naming Every Permitted Subtype Is Exhaustive, and Only Unguarded Cases Count
A Switch Statement With Patterns Must Be Exhaustive Too
null Matches Only case null; Neither default Nor case Object Does

gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-number-before-integer: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-number-before-integer: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-number-before-integer: Option a is supported by: 'An unguarded case dominates every later case of its own type or a subtype, guarded or not: `case Integer i` followed by `case Integer i when i > 100` gets the same error.' Integer is a subtype of Number, and the page also shows the javac error 'this case label is dominated by a preceding case label'.
recorded.prompt:q-two-guards-on-deploy: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-two-guards-on-deploy: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-two-guards-on-deploy: Option c is supported by: 'A guarded case covers nothing, unless its guard is the constant `true`.' The GuardOnly example then fails with 'the switch expression does not cover all possible input values'.
recorded.prompt:q-statement-over-payload: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-statement-over-payload: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-statement-over-payload: Option c is supported by: 'As soon as a statement uses a pattern, or `case null`, it gets the expression's rule.' The page shows the error 'the switch statement does not cover all possible input values'. It also says that over Object, 'cases for `String` and `Integer` alone are refused; the switch needs a `default` or a `case Object o`.'
recorded.prompt:q-object-case-and-null: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-object-case-and-null: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-object-case-and-null: Option d is supported by: 'a `null` selector throws before any case is tried, unless the switch has `case null`.' The page also shows 'replayObject(null) -> threw java.lang.NullPointerException'.

recorded.prompt:q-number-before-integer:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-number-before-integer:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-number-before-integer:b: Ruled out by 'Nothing ranks cases by how specific they are, the way overload resolution ranks methods: order is the only priority.' The dominance passage also says the code does not compile.
recorded.prompt:q-number-before-integer:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-number-before-integer:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-number-before-integer:c: Ruled out by the dominance passage ('An unguarded case dominates every later case of its own type or a subtype, guarded or not'), so the class does not compile. This option is partly true: cases are tried in order, and the page does say 'the compiler doesn't evaluate guards'. Only the outcome it draws is wrong.
recorded.prompt:q-number-before-integer:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-number-before-integer:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-number-before-integer:d: Ruled out by the router: `case Charge c -> "charges";` (unguarded) comes before `case Refund r when ...` (guarded), and the page says it compiles. The page also limits the ordering rule to one type: 'Within one type, write the guarded cases in priority order and the unguarded case last.'
recorded.prompt:q-two-guards-on-deploy:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-two-guards-on-deploy:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-two-guards-on-deploy:a: Ruled out by 'The compiler doesn't try to prove that the guards together accept every square.' This option is partly true: the two guards really do accept every Deploy between them.
recorded.prompt:q-two-guards-on-deploy:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-two-guards-on-deploy:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-two-guards-on-deploy:b: Ruled out by the heading '...Only Unguarded Cases Count' and by the reference table: 'every permitted subtype has an unguarded case'. This option is partly true: Job is sealed and every permitted type does have a case.

recorded.pass:q-two-guards-on-deploy:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-two-guards-on-deploy:d: Ruled out by `case Integer i when i > 0` followed by `case Integer i when i > 100`, which the page says 'compile without a warning'. The reference table also says 'a guarded case before a guarded case it overlaps | none: compiles'.

recorded.pass:q-statement-over-payload:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-statement-over-payload:a: Ruled out by the same 'gets the expression's rule' passage. This option is partly true: the page says a classic statement over an enum that skips a constant 'runs nothing'.
recorded.prompt:q-statement-over-payload:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-statement-over-payload:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-statement-over-payload:b: Ruled out because the switch does not build (the exhaustiveness error above). The page describes the hidden MatchException default only for a subtype added after compilation. It never says outright that javac adds that default only to switches it has found exhaustive, so the reasoning in the option's 'says' text is only implied by the page.
